course_description:
Build and integrate the knowledge and skills from different courses in the program and apply these in the optimisation of medicine use in the individual patient. New knowledge is acquired through evaluating evidence for drug use in all aspects of pharmacy and then integrated to develop the skills to identify and resolve drug related problems in consumers in a problem-based learning format. This course commences in week 5 of semester.

Apply your knowledge about medicines and pharmacy to the care of individual patients. The course will expose you to a range of clinical scenarios that reflect contemporary and future pharmacy practice. You will be required to demonstrate an ability to communicate, problem solve and integrate and apply knowledge from previous years of the Pharmacy program to optimise the use of medicines in patients in all aspects of care, including demonstrating patient-centred clinical, ethical and legal knowledge. This approach will help with the transition from student to a competent intern pharmacist who practices safely.

course_aims: To optimise medicines use in patients through integration and application of pharmacy knowledge and skills in a range of over-the-counter and prescription medicine scenarios that reflect contemporary and future pharmacy practice.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply expert knowledge of medicines gained throughout the program to improve person-centred health outcomes and reduce the risk of medicine-related harm to patients.

Use effective communication skills to comprehensively consult patients and clinicians (healthcare professionals) with patient-centred medicine information and care in a range of simulated pharmacy practice scenarios.
Identify, evaluate and justify the clinical significance of medication related problems in complex patient case scenarios.

Develop patient-centred medication management plans to resolve medication-related problems in complex patient case scenarios by referring to evidence-based clinical evidence (literature and tools) and the patient's context and goals.
Contribute to team-based care by expertly communicating and working with other members of the healthcare team in complex patient case scenarios.
Apply a model of ethical decision making to identify and propose practical, patient-centred solutions to ethical problems in complex patient case scenarios.
Demonstrate teamwork behaviours as appropriate to the roles of pharmacists within health care teams, including oral and written communication.

You will identify and prioritise any medication-related problems for the patient and provide a cohesive, detailed plan with appropriate monitoring to resolve the medication-related problems in a patient-centred, holistic approach. The document you are providing will be written to communicate these clinical recommendations you would like another health professional and/or a team of health professionals to implement in practice. assessment_details.title: Over-the-counter (OTC) and Ethics OSCE oral exam
assessment_details.task_description: The PHRM4012 OSCE oral exam will consist of 3 OSCE stations: Over-the-counter counselling station, product request (5 minutes) Over-the-counter counselling station, symptom-based request (5 minutes) Ethics station (10 minutes) Further descriptions, guidance and marking criteria for these stations are available on the PHRM4012 Blackboard site. The PHRM4012 OSCE stations will be based on concepts, medicine disease states, medicines, scenarios, skills and knowledge you have attained during your pharmacy degree. This Oral Exam will be recorded, and the resulting recording retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application. assessment_details.title: Patient centred case oral examination (VIVA)
assessment_details.task_description: The oral examination will assess knowledge and application to identify medication related problems and discuss therapeutic decision making in choosing options to resolve the medication related problems. This will be an oral VIVA of a patient case during the end of semester examination period. The viva will be 25 minutes in duration including 10 minutes reading and preparation time. During the preparation and reading time only, you will have access to the AMH and eTGs. You will need to bring your own physical hard copy of the AMH. You will then commence the oral examination which lasts 15 minutes, discussing the medication related problem(s) you have identified and plan to resolve these with the examiner who will then also ask you questions about your case and recommendations. This oral viva will be recorded and retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 5 To Week 11
learning_activities.topic: Practice roleplay (OTC) simulation OTC practice cases and OTC notes will be provided on the course site for students to undertake self-directed practice. On tutorial weeks the course coordinator will be available for 1hr after the tutorial in the same room to answer questions. Students are encouraged to practice taking a patient history and counselling their simulation patient during their study time with these cases. The aim of these cases is to will allow students to practice and hone their skills in medication history taking and counselling for over-the-counter ailments and products in role play activities with or without their peers. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 5 To Week 11
learning_activities.topic: Skills Modules Content for the weekly skills modules will be available on the course site to allow students to undertake self-directed learning on three topics; ethics, communication, and pharmaceutical calculations. On tutorial weeks the course coordinator will be available for 1hr after the tutorial in the same room to answer questions. Skills modules are aimed at improving core pharmacy practice skills. They will include modules on assertive communication strategies in difficult professional situations, educating patients on medicines and devices, discussing ethical dilemmas applying an ethical framework to decision making, and applying knowledge of pharmacy calculations to derive appropriate formulations and safe dosing recommendations. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 5 To Week 12
learning_activities.topic: Patient Centred Integrated Cases Participants will work in small groups on complex patient cases to identify and assess medication-related problems, the reason for the problem, develop and review a management plan for the patient including research of evidence in the literature to consider other options to resolve the problem and justify your management plan. Participants will also be expected to discuss the role of other key healthcare professionals and communicate medication-related problems and solutions to improve the care of the patient in the case. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05, L07
